source_text: ΛΟΓΟΣ ΛΔʹ. Εἰς τοὺς Αἰγύπτου ἐπιδημήσαντας. Αʹ. Τοὺς ἀπ' Αἰγύπτου προσφθέγξομαι, δίκαιον γάρ· ἐπειδὴ καὶ προθύμως συνεληλύθασι, τῷ ζήλῳ τὸν φθόνον νικήσαντες, Αἰγύπτου ταύτης, ἣν πλουτίζει μὲν ποταμὸς ἐκ γῆς ὕων, καὶ πελαγίζων ὥρια ἵνα καὶ αὐτὸς μικρόν τι μιμήσωμαι τοὺς περὶ ταῦτα κομψούς· πλουτίζει δὲ Χριστὸς ὁ ἐμὸς, πρότερον μὲν εἰς Αἴγυπτον φυγαδευόμενος, νυνὶ δὲ ἀπ' Αἰγύπτου χορηγούμενος· τότε μὲν, ἐκ τῆς Ἡρώδου παιδοφονίας, νῦν δὲ, ἐκ τῆς τῶν πατέρων φιλοτεκνίας· Χριστὸς, ἡ καινὴ τροφὴ τῶν καλῶς πεινώντων, ἡ μείζων σιτοδοσία πάσης τῆς ἱστορουμένης τε καὶ πιστευομένης· ὁ ἅρτος, ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβαίνων, καὶ ζωὴν διδοὺς τῷ κόσμῳ, τὴν ἀνόλεθρόν τε καὶ ἀκατάλυτον, περὶ οὗ καὶ νῦν ἀκούειν δοκῶ μοι λέγοντος τοῦ Πατρός· Ἐξ Αἰγύπτου ἐκάλεσα τὸν Υἱόν μου. Βʹ. Ἀφ' ὑμῶν γὰρ ἐξήχηται ὁ λόγος εἰς πάντας ἀν θρώπους, ὑγιῶς πιστευόμενός τε καὶ κηρυσσόμενος καὶ ὑμεῖς ἄριστοι καρποδόται πάντων, μάλιστα τῶν νῦν ὀρθῶς πιστευόντων, ὅσα ἐμὲ γινώσκειν, τὸν τῆς τοιαύτης τροφῆς, οὐκ ἐραστὴν μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ χορηγὸν, καὶ οὐκ ἔνδημον μόνον, ἀλλ' ἤδη καὶ ὑπερ όριον. Ὑμεῖς γὰρ τρέφετε μὲν σωματικῶς δήμους καὶ πόλεις, ἐφ' ὅσον ἐξικνεῖται ὑμῶν τὸ φιλάνθρω πον· τρέφετε δὲ πνευματικῶς, οὐ τὸν δεῖνα δῆμον, οὐδὲ τήνδε, ἢ τήνδε τὴν πόλιν μικροῖς ὁρίοις περιγραφομένην, κἂν φρονῶσιν ὑπέρλαμπρον, ἀλλὰ μικροῦ πᾶσαν τὴν οἰκουμένην. Καὶ θεραπεύετε, οὐ λιμὸν ἄρτου, οὐδὲ δίψαν ὕδατος, ἃ καὶ λιμώττειν οὐ μέγα, καὶ μὴ λιμώττειν ῥᾴδιον· ἀλλὰ λιμὸν τοῦ ἀκοῦσαι λόγου Κυρίου, ὃν καὶ πάσχειν ἐλεεινότατον, καὶ θεραπεύειν νῦν ἐργωδέστατον· ἐπειδὴ ἐπληθύνθη ἡ ἀνομία, καὶ ὀλίγους εὑρίσκω τοὺς γνησίους ταύτης θεραπευτάς. Γʹ. Τοιοῦτος Ἰωσὴφ ὁ ὑμέτερος σιτομέτρης, ταυτὸν δὲ εἰπεῖν καὶ ἡμέτερος, ὃς καὶ προβλέπειν ᾔδει λιμὸν ὑπὸ σοφίας ὑπερβαλλούσης, καὶ θεραπεύειν λόγοις οἰκονομίας, ταῖς καλαῖς τῶν βοῶν καὶ πίοσι, τὰς αἰσχρὰς καὶ ἀτρόφους ἰώμενος. Καὶ Ἰωσὴφ ὁπότερον βούλει λαμβάνειν, εἴτε τὸν τῆς ἀθανασίας ἐραστὴν, καὶ δημιουργὸν, καὶ ἐπώνυμον· εἴτε τὸν ἐκείνου καὶ θρόνῳ, καὶ λόγῳ, καὶ πολιᾷ διάδοχον, τὸν νέον Πέτρον ἡμῖν, οὐχ ἧττον τὴν ἀρετὴν, ἢ τὴν κλῆσιν· ὑφ' ὧν τὸ μέσον ἐξεκόπη καὶ συνετρίβη, κἂν ἔτι σπαίρῃ μικρά τε καὶ ἀσθενῆ, καθάπερ τὸ οὐραῖον διακοπέντος τοῦ ὄφεως· ὧν ὁ μὲν ἐν γήρᾳ καλῷ καταλύσας τὸν βίον ἐπὶ πολλοῖς τοῖς ἀγωνίσμασι καὶ ἀθλήμασιν, ἄνωθεν ἐποπτεύει, εὖ οἶδα, νῦν τὰ ἡμέτερα, καὶ χεῖρα ὀρέγει τοῖς ὑπὲρ τοῦ καλοῦ κάμνουσι, καὶ τόσῳ μᾶλλον, ὅσῳ τῶν δεσμῶν ἐστιν ἐλεύθερος· ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν αὐτὴν κατάλυσιν, ἢ ἀνάλυσιν, ἐπὶ τοῖς αὐτοῖς ἄθλοις ἐπείγεται, καὶ πλησιάζει μὲν ἤδη τοῖς ἄνω, τοσοῦ τον δὲ μετὰ τῆς σαρκός ἐστιν ἔτι, ὅσον βοηθῆσαι τῷ λόγῳ τὰ τελευταῖα, καὶ τῆς ὁδοῦ γενέσθαι μετὰ δαψιλεστέρων τῶν ἐφοδίων. Δʹ. Τούτων ὑμεῖς θρέμματα καὶ προβλήματα τῶν μεγάλων, καὶ δογματιστῶν, καὶ ἀγωνιστῶν τῆς ἀλη θείας, καὶ νικητῶν· οὓς οὐ καιρὸς, οὐ δυνάστης, οὐ λόγος, οὐ φθόνος, οὐ φόβος, οὐ κατήγορος, οὐ συκοφάντης, οὐ φανερῶς πολεμῶν, οὐ λαθραίως ἐπιβουλεύων, οὐχ ἡμέτερος τῷ δοκεῖν, οὐκ ἀλλότριος, οὐ χρυσὸς, ὁ ἀφανὴς τύραννος, ᾧ νῦν τὰ πολλὰ μεταῤῥίπτεται καὶ πεττεύεται, οὐ θεραπεῖαι, οὐκ ἀπειλαὶ, οὐκ ἐξορίαι μακραί τε καὶ ἀριθμούμεναι (δημεύσει γὰρ οὐκ ἐγένοντο μόνον ἁλωτοὶ, διὰ τὸν μέγαν πλοῦ τον, τὴν ἀκτημοσύνην), οὐκ ἄλλο οὐδὲν τῶν ἀπόντων, ἢ τῶν παρόντων, ἢ τῶν προσδοκωμένων ἐπῆρεν, οὐδὲ ἀνέπεισε χείρους γενέσθαι, καὶ προδοῦναί τι τῆς Τριάδος, καὶ ζημιωθῆναι θεότητα.
thought_title: Welcoming Egyptians who bring true teaching
orientation: Gregory greets visitors from Egypt as fellow orthodox believers whose confession feeds the church.
pass_a_gloss: Word 34. To those who have sojourned from Egypt. 1. I will address those from Egypt, for it is just; since they have also come together eagerly, having conquered envy by zeal, from this Egypt, which on the one hand a river enriches raining from earth and making sea in season so that I myself also may imitate in a small way those clever in these matters; and on the other hand Christ who is mine enriches, formerly on the one hand being driven in flight into Egypt, now on the other hand being supplied from Egypt; then on the one hand from the child killing of Herod, now on the other hand from the love for children of the fathers; Christ, the new food of those hungering in a good way, the greatest food distribution of all that is recorded and believed; the bread, the one coming down from heaven and giving life to the world, the life that is imperishable and indissoluble, concerning whom also now I think I hear the Father saying: From Egypt I called my Son. 2. For from you the word has sounded out to all men, being believed in a sound way and proclaimed, and you are best givers of fruit of all, most of all of those now believing rightly, as far as I know, me who am of such food not only a lover but also a supplier, and not only dwelling in the land but already also beyond the boundary. For you feed in a bodily way peoples and cities, as far as your love for men reaches; and you feed in a spiritual way, not this or that people, nor this or that city bounded by small boundaries, even if they think overly splendid things, but almost all the inhabited world. And you heal, not famine of bread, nor thirst of water, which both to hunger is not great, and not to hunger is easy; but famine of hearing the word of the Lord, which both to suffer is most pitiable, and to heal now is most laborious; since lawlessness has been multiplied, and I find few genuine healers of this famine. 3. Such is Joseph your measurer of grain, and to say the same thing also ours, who both knew how to foresee famine by surpassing wisdom, and to heal by words of stewardship, healing by the good and fat cows the shameful and unfed cows. And take Joseph in whichever way you wish to take him, either the lover and maker and namesake of immortality; or his successor both in throne and in word and in grey hair, our new Peter, not less in virtue than in calling; by whom the middle has been cut out and crushed, even if it still writhes in small and weak form, just as the tail when the snake has been cut through; of whom the one having ended life in good old age upon many contests and struggles, watches from above, I know well, now our affairs, and stretches a hand to those laboring for the good, and by so much more as he is free from bonds; and the other hastens to the same lodging, or release, upon the same struggles, and already draws near to those above, and is with the flesh still by so much as to help the word with last things, and to become of the way with more abundant provisions. 4. Of these great ones, and teachers of doctrine, and fighters for truth, and conquerors, you are nurslings and offspring; whom neither time, nor ruler, nor speech, nor envy, nor fear, nor accuser, nor false informer, nor one warring openly, nor one plotting secretly, nor one of ours in seeming, nor stranger, nor gold, the unseen tyrant, by which now most things are turned and moved as pieces in a game, nor attentions, nor threats, nor exiles long and counted (for by confiscation they did not become only catchable, on account of great wealth, which is poverty in possessions), nor anything else of things absent, or of things present, or of things expected, moved, nor persuaded to become worse, and to betray something of the Trinity, and to be deprived of divinity.

pass_b_english: I will address those who have come from Egypt, and it is right to do so. They have gathered here eagerly, with zeal overcoming envy. I mean this Egypt, which a river enriches by raining up out of the earth and spreading wide in its season, to borrow a little, myself, from those who write cleverly about such things. Yet my Christ enriches it still more. He once fled into Egypt, and now he is supplied from Egypt. Then he fled from Herod's murder of the children; now he is given from the fathers' love for their children. He is Christ, the new food for those who hunger well, the greatest food distribution of any ever recorded or believed. He is "the bread that comes down from heaven and gives life to the world" (John 6:33), a life that cannot perish or be destroyed. About him I think I now hear the Father saying, "Out of Egypt I called my Son" (Hosea 11:1).

For "the word has sounded out from you to all people" (1 Thessalonians 1:8), soundly believed and soundly preached. And you are the finest fruit-bearers of all, especially among those who now believe rightly, as far as I know. For I myself, with regard to such food, am not only a lover but also a supplier, and not only a native but already one beyond the border.

For you feed peoples and cities bodily, as far as your kindness reaches. Yet you also feed spiritually, and not some particular people, nor this or that city bounded by small limits, even if they think most splendidly of themselves, but almost the whole world. And you heal, not a famine of bread nor a thirst for water, for to hunger for these is no great thing and not to hunger for them is easy. You heal "a famine of hearing the word of the Lord" (Amos 8:11). To suffer that famine is most pitiable, and to heal it now is most laborious, "for lawlessness has multiplied" (Matthew 24:12), and I find few genuine healers of it.

Such is your Joseph, the measurer of grain, and ours too, I may say. In surpassing wisdom he knew how to foresee famine, and by prudent stewardship he knew how to heal it with words, using the fine, fattened cows to remedy the ugly, starved ones. Take Joseph in whichever sense you wish: either the lover and maker of immortality, and the one named for it, or his successor in throne and word and grey hair, our new Peter, no less in virtue than in name. By these two men the middle party was cut out and crushed, even if it still writhes in small and weak form, just as the tail does when the snake has been cut through. One of them ended his life in a good old age after many contests and trials, and now watches over our affairs from above, I know well. He stretches out his hand to those who labor for the good, and all the more because he is free from his bonds. The other hastens toward the same lodging, or release, amid the same labors. He already draws near to those above, yet he remains in the flesh just long enough to help the message one last time and to make his journey with richer provisions.

You are the nurslings and bulwarks of these great men, teachers of doctrine and champions and victors for the truth. Neither time nor ruler moved them, neither argument nor envy nor fear, neither accuser nor slanderer, neither open enemy nor secret plotter, neither seeming friend nor stranger. Neither did gold, that hidden tyrant by which now most things are turned and moved as pieces in a game. Neither favors nor threats nor long and repeated exiles moved them, for they could not be caught by confiscation alone, since their great wealth was having nothing. Nothing else, absent or present or expected, lifted them or persuaded them to become worse, to betray anything of the Trinity, and to be deprived of divinity.
notes: Print spacing splits ἀνθρώπους, ὑπερόριον, φιλάνθρωπον, ἀληθείας; read as single words.

problems.why: πρόβλημα means a bulwark or what is put forward, not an offshoot.
problems.ruling: προβλήματα means bulwarks/defenses (what is put forward), paired with θρέμματα; 'offshoots' misses the protective sense and misleads readers about the Egyptians' role.

edits.old: You are the nurslings and offshoots of these great men
edits.new: You are the nurslings and bulwarks of these great men

fixed: nurslings and offshoots -> nurslings and bulwarks: probálēma (προβλήματα, from προβάλλω) means bulwark/defence put forward, not offshoot; fixed

problems.quote: believed in sound health and preached in sound health
problems.why: ὑγιῶς means soundly, in sound doctrine, not physical health.
problems.ruling: ὑγιῶς means soundly/correctly (of faith and preaching); 'in sound health' misleads toward physical health. Should be 'soundly' or 'in sound doctrine'.

edits.old: believed in sound health and preached in sound health

fixed: mistranslation 'in sound health' fixed: source ὑγιῶς means soundly/in sound doctrine, not physical health, with πιστευομένός τε καὶ κηρυσσόμενος.
earlier 'bulwarks' left alone - correct: source θρέμματα καὶ προβλήματα means nurslings and bulwarks/projections, not offshoots.

last_rejected.quote: by prudent stewardship he knew how to heal it with words
last_rejected.why: One dative: he heals by the plans of his stewardship, not by speech plus a separate stewardship.
last_rejected.fix: and by the plans of his stewardship he knew how to heal it, curing the ugly, starved cows with the fine, fat ones.
last_rejected.ruling: 'θεραπεύειν λόγοις οἰκονομίας' is rendered as healing with words through stewardship. This stays within the range of the genitive and does not change the sense.

last_rejected.quote: Nothing else, absent or present or expected, lifted them or persuaded them to become worse
last_rejected.source_quote: οὓς οὐ καιρός, οὐ δυνάστης, οὐ λόγος, οὐ φθόνος, οὐ φόβος, οὐ κατήγορος, οὐ συκοφάντης, οὐ φανερῶς πολεμῶν, οὐ λαθραίως ἐπιβουλεύων, οὐχ ἡμέτερος τῷ δοκεῖν, οὐκ ἀλλότριος, οὐ χρυσός, ὁ ἀφανὴς τύραννος, ᾧ νῦν τὰ πολλὰ μεταῤῥίπτεται καὶ πεττεύεται, οὐ θεραπεῖαι, οὐκ ἀπειλαί, οὐκ ἐξόριαι μακραί τε καὶ ἀριθμούμεναι, οὐκ ἄλλο οὐδὲν τῶν ἀπόντων, ἢ τῶν παρόντων, ἢ τῶν προσδοκωμένων ἐπῆρεν, οὐδὲ ἀνέπεισε χείρους γενέσθαι, καὶ προδοῦναί τι τῆς Τριάδος, καὶ ζημιωθῆναι θεότητα
last_rejected.why: One verb pair governs the whole list. 'Else' confines the betrayal and loss of divinity to unnamed things.
last_rejected.fix: None of these, nor anything else absent, present, or expected, lifted them or persuaded them to become worse, betray anything of the Trinity, and lose divinity.
last_rejected.ruling: Source has 'οὐκ ἄλλο οὐδὲν', so 'Nothing else' is literal. 'ἐπῆρεν... ἀνέπεισε' are rendered as 'lifted... persuaded', and the list is covered. No loss of meaning.

last_rejected.quote: For I myself, with regard to such food, am not only a lover but also a supplier, and not only a native but already one beyond the border.
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸν τῆς τοιαύτης τροφῆς, οὐκ ἐραστὴν μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ χορηγὸν, καὶ οὐκ ἔνδημον μόνον, ἀλλ' ἤδη καὶ ὑπερόριον
last_rejected.why: The source has no first-person 'I'. The accusative phrase continues the praise of the Egyptians as givers of fruit to the believer who loves and supplies such food. The English makes Gregory the subject.
last_rejected.fix: …especially to those who now believe rightly, as far as I know: the one who is not only a lover of such food but also its supplier, not only local but already beyond the border.
last_rejected.ruling: Accusative τὸν…ἐραστήν…χορηγὸν…ὑπερόριον agrees with ἐμέ in ὅσα ἐμὲ γινώσκειν, so Gregory is the subject.
